subject: Climate & Environment
title: Radon: The Invisible Gas
description: A quick win: understand Radon: The Invisible Gas.

hook.text: Radon is a radioactive gas that seeps into homes from the ground. You cannot smell or see it.

buildup.text: It comes from natural uranium decay in soil and rock beneath buildings.

discovery.text: Radon is the second leading cause of lung cancer after smoking — killing 21,000 Americans yearly.

twist.text: Any home can have elevated radon — geography, not building age, determines the risk.

climax.text: A simple $15 test kit can measure radon. Mitigation systems fix the problem permanently.

punchline.text: A $15 test could save your lungs from a silent threat underfoot.

quiz.question: What is radon's rank among causes of lung cancer?

details.summary: Radon is a naturally occurring radioactive gas that seeps from soil and rock into buildings through cracks and foundations. It is the second leading cause of lung cancer after smoking, responsible for roughly 21,000 US lung cancer deaths per year.
details.whyItMatters: Radon is present in homes worldwide and testing is cheap and easy. Awareness directly saves lives because mitigation systems can reduce levels by over 99 percent.
takeaways: Radon forms from the natural decay of uranium in soil and rock
It is the second leading cause of lung cancer after smoking
Simple mitigation systems can reduce indoor radon by over 99 percent

faq.question: How do you test for radon in your home?
faq.answer: Short-term test kits are available at hardware stores for under 20 dollars. You place the detector in the lowest lived-in level for 2 to 7 days, then mail it to a lab. Long-term tests over 90 days give a more accurate annual average.

faq.question: How does radon mitigation work in a home?
faq.answer: The most common method is sub-slab depressurization, where a pipe and fan system draws radon from beneath the foundation and vents it above the roofline. This typically reduces indoor radon levels by 95 to 99 percent.
